annotations.text:
The name: two research rounds, 52 candidates, 12 fully vetted against the App Store, USPTO, domains, and dark associations.

Hushlight won as the only name with zero exact-name apps in either store, no software or health trademark, and lullaby warmth built in - it names the object this identity turns the app into: a small warm lamp at 3am.

Runner-up: Soonrise (also fully clear; trades the lamp for the dawn promise, but blurs into 'sunrise' when spoken).

Every warm dictionary word tried in round 1 (Soon, Lull, Exhale, Steady, Held) was already mined out by existing apps.

How this direction was chosen: three identities were drafted and scored against the 3am-labor reality. Nightstand won (44/50) over First Light (43) and Slack Tide (33) - it is the only one designed primarily for the moment the app earns its existence: night. First Light's export report, crash-safe timer, merge affordance and dawn choreography are folded in.
Core flow, night theme (the default room). Labor mostly ramps at night - dark is the identity, not a variant. Nothing red exists anywhere in the shipped app.
Daytime is a first-class translation: same room with the curtains open - warm paper, deep amber ink. Not an inverted afterthought.

The runner-up direction, kept for comparison: First Light - sunrise neutrals, rose live-state, light-first. Scored one point behind Nightstand; its warmth survives as grafts in the winner. Its rose live-state (visible on this tape) drifting toward warm-red was one of the reasons it lost.
